hints.title: Three Segment Reversal Symmetry
hints.text: Rotating an array right by k steps moves the last k elements to the front while shifting the first n minus k elements to the back.

hints.title: Reverse Whole And Halves Invariant
hints.text: Reversing the entire array places the target segments in their final areas, after which reversing each segment restores their original internal order.

hints.title: Three Stage In Place Reversal Procedure
hints.text: Normalize k by taking modulo array length. Reverse the entire array from 0 to n minus one. Next, reverse the prefix from 0 to k minus one. Finally, reverse the suffix from k to n minus one.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def rotate(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> None:
        n = len(nums)
        k %= n
        def reverse(l: int, r: int):
            while l < r:
                nums[l], nums[r] = nums[r], nums[l]
                l += 1
                r -= 1
        reverse(0, n - 1)
        reverse(0, k - 1)
        reverse(k, n - 1)
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rotating one step at a time takes O(N * K) quadratic time, while allocating a second array consumes O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The three-reversal method modifies elements in place in O(N) time and requires strictly O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should normalize k modulo n and implement the three-pass reversal algorithm in place without extra arrays.
